summary: No reachable vulnerabilities. Tampered meta record: the only untrusted input is the local IndexedDB 'meta' record (same-origin, user-controlled). It is read back through parsePersistentStorage, which accepts only a plain non-array object with a boolean 'granted' and returns null otherwise; structured-clone values cannot carry getters, so no code runs on read. The worst a tampered record does is skip or repeat the one persist() request, which is advisory and has no security effect. Upgrade: the v5 step only creates the empty META_STORE under 'oldVersion < 5'; earlier stores and records are untouched, and onversionchange still closes older connections, so existing data is not lost. Failure handling: requestPersistenceOnce wraps the read, persist() (sync throw or rejection, which counts as not granted) and the write in separate try/catch blocks and never rejects. main.tsx calls it with 'void' after render(), outside React, so no failure can produce an error boundary, stuck screen or unhandled rejection. If persist() never settles, only the background promise waits. browserPersist guards a missing navigator.storage or persist and calls persist as a method. Logs contain fixed messages and the error object only. There are no secrets, no network calls, no new dependencies and no randomness.
